themes.label: Default stance and who decides
themes.desc: Whether AI is allowed by default, who sets the rule (department, instructor, assignment), and whether uses are sorted into levels or categories.

themes.label: Communicating expectations
themes.desc: How and where the rules are made explicit to students.

themes.label: What students may use AI for
themes.desc: Uses that are allowed or encouraged: explanation, debugging help, brainstorming, writing support, course-provided tools.

themes.label: What students may not use AI for
themes.desc: Uses that are ruled out, especially generating code or solutions that are submitted as one's own.

themes.label: Disclosure and attribution
themes.desc: Whether and how AI use must be acknowledged, cited, or documented (prompts, transcripts, reflections).

themes.label: Student accountability and understanding
themes.desc: Students remain responsible for what they submit and must be able to explain and defend it.

themes.label: Assessment design
themes.desc: How assignments, exams, weighting, and formats change in response to AI.

themes.label: Detection and enforcement
themes.desc: Detectors, evidence, academic-integrity processes, sanctions, and amnesty.

themes.label: Why: learning and careers
themes.desc: The reasons given: protecting skill-building and productive struggle, and preparing students for AI-rich professional work.

themes.label: Faculty and staff use of AI
themes.desc: AI use by instructors and TAs for grading, feedback, materials, and course operations.

themes.label: Equity, privacy, ethics, and IP
themes.desc: Access and cost, data and privacy, bias and environmental concerns, and intellectual property.

themes.label: Governance and change over time
themes.desc: Acknowledging that policy will change, review cycles, and who maintains the policy.

phases.label: Before the course
phases.desc: Decisions instructors and departments make while designing the course and its policy.

phases.label: At the start of the course
phases.desc: Communicating expectations to students up front.

phases.label: While students work
phases.desc: Rules that apply while doing assignments, labs, and projects.

phases.label: During assessment
phases.desc: Exams, quizzes, interviews, and other evaluations of individual understanding.

phases.label: When something goes wrong
phases.desc: Suspected misuse, detection, evidence, consequences, and amnesty.

phases.label: Over time
phases.desc: Reflection, review, and revision of the policy as tools and practice change.

actors.label: Addressed to students
actors.desc: Rules and expectations students must follow.

actors.label: Addressed to instructors
actors.desc: Guidance and obligations for faculty designing and running courses.

actors.label: Addressed to TAs and staff
actors.desc: Guidance for teaching assistants, graders, and support staff.

actors.label: Department commitments
actors.desc: What the unit itself commits to or decides.

codebook.label: Default stance
codebook.definition: Whether AI use is allowed or prohibited when nothing else is specified.

codebook.label: Instructor discretion
codebook.definition: The instructor (or assignment) sets the rule; the unit defers to course-level decisions.

codebook.label: Use categories / levels
codebook.definition: Explicit tiers or categories of permitted use (e.g. no AI, limited AI, open AI).

codebook.label: Syllabus communication
codebook.definition: Requirements to state AI expectations in the syllabus or at the start of an assignment.

codebook.label: Permitted uses
codebook.definition: Specific uses of AI that are allowed or encouraged.

codebook.label: Writing assistance
codebook.definition: AI for prose: reports, documentation, editing, grammar.

codebook.label: Course-provided tools
codebook.definition: AI tools supplied or sanctioned by the course or institution (e.g. a course tutor bot).

codebook.label: Prohibited uses
codebook.definition: Specific uses of AI that are not allowed.

codebook.label: Code generation
codebook.definition: Provisions specifically about AI-generated code (Copilot, ChatGPT code).

codebook.label: Disclosure and citation
codebook.definition: Requirements to acknowledge, cite, or document AI use.

codebook.label: Accountability and understanding
codebook.definition: Students are responsible for submitted work and must understand and be able to explain it.

codebook.label: Assessment design
codebook.definition: Changes to assignments, grading weight, or evaluation formats in response to AI.

codebook.label: In-person / proctored exams
codebook.definition: Use of supervised, oral, or in-person evaluation to assess individual understanding.

codebook.label: Detection tools
codebook.definition: Statements about AI detectors, their reliability, or their use.

codebook.label: Integrity and sanctions
codebook.definition: Treatment of misuse as an academic-integrity violation; consequences; amnesty or regret clauses.

codebook.label: Learning rationale
codebook.definition: Reasons grounded in learning: skill-building, practice, productive struggle.

codebook.label: AI literacy and careers
codebook.definition: Preparing students to use AI well, critically, or professionally.

codebook.label: Collaboration analogy
codebook.definition: Treating AI like a person, collaborator, tutor, or other source under existing collaboration rules.

codebook.label: Instructor / staff use
codebook.definition: General statements about AI use by faculty, TAs, or staff.

codebook.label: Faculty grading and feedback
codebook.definition: AI in grading, feedback, or evaluation of student work by instructors or TAs.

codebook.label: Faculty course materials
codebook.definition: AI in creating course content, assignments, or examples.

codebook.label: Equity and access
codebook.definition: Unequal access, paid tools, accessibility, fairness across students.

codebook.label: Privacy and data
codebook.definition: Uploading student work or course materials, FERPA, data retention, approved tools.

codebook.label: Ethics, bias, environment
codebook.definition: Bias, hallucination, harms, environmental and labor concerns.

codebook.label: Intellectual property
codebook.definition: Licensing, ownership, and copyright of AI-generated output or course materials.

codebook.label: Policy evolution
codebook.definition: Policy may change; review cycles; ongoing deliberation.

codebook.label: Research use
codebook.definition: AI in theses, research projects, or graduate work.
